category_specific_evidence: Issue #4517 reproducer: scipy.special.jv(0,0) - 1j*scipy.special.yn(0,0) returns (nan+inf*j), flagged as the incorrect result.
The issue comment states that nan+infj is a valid C99 complex infinity representation, and that the AMOS codes do not compute non-finite results so overflow needs hardcoding.
DLMF 10.7.2 asymptotic H_0^(2)(z) ~ -(2i/pi) log z = -(2i/pi)[log|z| + i Arg(z)] shows the real part depends on the direction of approach to zero.
Discussion reports hankel2(0, 1e-100) = 1+146.66j and hankel2(0, -1e-100) = 3+146.66j, and notes the asymptotic formula is missing a real-part offset of 1.
The merged patch sets cy.real(NAN) and cy.imag(INFINITY) for v == 0 and z == 0, and the added test asserts np.isnan(res.real) and np.isposinf(res.imag).

A discussion revision proposed asserting res.real == 1 with imaginary part +inf, which conflicts with the final NaN real-part choice; the passages do not settle which is the final expected value beyond the committed patch and test.
reproduction_risks: The expected real part is contested: the patch and test use NaN, while an earlier suggestion used 1.0 and another comment argues the real part should depend on approach direction.
The PR states it assumes the definition in terms of J_n and Y_n is appropriate, so the expected value rests on that definition.
Values near zero (1e-100) show a real-part offset that does not match the asymptotic formula, so direction-dependent checks may disagree with the implementation.
